hints: A route from 1 to n may be impossible if n is not reachable.
A DAG has a topological order, so longest-path values can be computed from earlier vertices to later ones.
Store a predecessor whenever a longer path to a vertex is found.
analogy: Process a flight network in dependency order; each city keeps the longest route reaching it so far.
example: In a chain 1->2->4, the longest route has three cities and is reconstructed via parents.
algorithm: Topologically sort the graph. Set best[1]=1; for each reachable u, relax best[v]=best[u]+1 on each edge. Reconstruct from n; output IMPOSSIBLE if unset.
correctness: Every directed path in a DAG follows topological order; when u is processed, all possible predecessor paths to u are known, so relaxation finds the longest path.
